title: Neti neti: not this, not this
hookLine: why would a teacher describe the self only by what it isn't?
carry: neti neti: the self is the one who sees
tomorrow: Om has three sounds. so what's the fourth part?

lines: NOT A CAFÉ, NOT A BAR.
NETI NETI: NOT THIS, NOT THIS.
cards: A friend asks what the new place in town is like, and the only answer anyone has is: not a café, not a bar, not really a bookstore either. As descriptions go, it's close to useless.
The Brihadaranyaka uses that exact move, on purpose, for the biggest thing it talks about. Asked about the self, Yajnavalkya answers King Janaka with two words, twice: neti neti. Not this, not this.
So why would a teacher describe something only by what it isn't?

teach.b: Here's the passage, in plain words. This great unborn self lives in the space within the heart, ruler of all, lord of all. It doesn't grow greater by good deeds, or smaller by bad ones.

teach.h: WHATEVER CAN BE SEEN: NOT THIS.
teach.b: This self is not this, not this. It can't be grasped, so it isn't grasped. It can't be broken, so it doesn't break.
It doesn't cling, so it isn't bound. It doesn't tremble, and it isn't harmed. Now the puzzle starts to solve itself.
Anything that can be pointed at, a thought, a feeling, a body, a role, is something the self can see. Whatever can be seen gets set aside: not this. The refusal isn't emptiness.
It keeps the self from being mistaken for one more item on the list. There's a second puzzle nearby.

teach.h: AS ONE ACTS, SO ONE BECOMES.
teach.b: Earlier in the same chapter, the text said: as one acts, so one becomes. So do deeds matter or not? The text joins the two itself.
Deeds shape the person who wants; the self beneath, it says, doesn't grow by deeds or shrink.

teach.h: CALM, AND THE SELF IN ALL.
teach.b: And the one who knows it, the next verse says, becomes calm, patient, collected, and sees the self in everything.

how: Advaita teachers often use 'neti neti' as a method of inquiry: setting aside body, mind and role one by one as things seen, to point at the self that sees.

o: this self is Brahman, known by setting aside what it isn't
a teaching that the self is the body alone
a vow to refuse every pleasure and every comfort

games.q: the self, by what it isn't. tap the pairs.
p: the self doesn't grow or shrink

s: neti neti means the self doesn't exist
it says the self can't be grasped like an object; the same verse calls it ruler of all, lord of all.
the passage says the self doesn't grow by good deeds or shrink by bad ones
Brihadaranyaka 4.4.22, with 4.4.23 saying the same of the knower's greatness.
the same chapter also says: as one acts, so one becomes
deeds shape the person who wants; the self beneath, the text says, is untouched.

games.q: a friend says: if the self isn't changed by good or bad deeds, why bother being good? what does this chapter actually hold?
o: it agrees: the self is untouched, so deeds don't really matter.
both: deeds shape the one who wants; the self beneath isn't changed.
only ritual deeds count; ordinary choices leave no mark.
games.why: the chapter says as one acts, so one becomes, and also that the self doesn't grow or shrink by deeds. the knower, it adds, becomes calm and patient.

practice: Pick one object within reach, a cup, a pen, your own hand, and name it silently. Then notice that you're the one seeing it, and set it aside: not this.
Do the same with whatever shows up next, a sound, a thought, and keep resting as the one who sees.

wordCard.voice: Ayam atma brahma, met through the back door: neti neti, not this, not this. The self, described by setting aside everything that can be pointed at.

orig.note: Sanskrit: not so, not so; read as 'not this, not this' (Brihadaranyaka 4.4.22).

carryVoice: Hold on to it: neti neti. Whatever you can point at, you are the one who sees it; that seer is the self. Same time tomorrow.

sources.ref: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 4.4.22 (this great unborn self, in the space within the heart, ruler of all, lord of all; not greater by good deeds, not less by bad; not this, not this; ungraspable, unbreakable, unattached, unbound, it does not tremble, it is not harmed)

Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 4.4.23 (the eternal greatness of the knower of Brahman does not grow by deeds or shrink; calm, restrained, withdrawn, patient, collected, he sees the self in the self and sees all as the self)
Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 4.4.5–6 (as one acts, so one becomes; so much for the one who desires; the one without desire, being Brahman, goes to Brahman)
